Context: i was trying to recall and describe what the hallway looked like and what i might have observed if i were a fly on the wall during that tenminute period to be honest i really didnt like it
Response: it seems like you had a negative experience while recalling the hallway and the events that happened during those ten minutes is there any particular reason or specific event that caused you to feel this way and if so would you feel comfortable sharing it with me

Context: recently my roommate accused me of some things and we ended up having a confrontation about breaking our lease i was confident in my argument and stood my ground and i felt proud of myself afterward however during the confrontation i was shaking and my hands and voice were trembling
Response: its great to hear that you were able to stand your ground and be assertive in such a challenging situation its natural for our bodies to exhibit physical signs of stress and anxiety like shaking and trembling in confrontational situations remember its important to communicate effectively and calmly in these situations to prevent further conflicts can you think of any strategies that might help you maintain a calmer demeanor in future confrontations

Context: i had a little altercation with someone and those who witnessed it told me that they hadnt seen that side of me in a long time im not sure how i managed to stand up to him like that
Response: it sounds like you were able to assert yourself in a challenging situation its interesting how we sometimes surprise ourselves with our reactions can you think of any factors or emotions that might have contributed to your response in this situation

Context: so this time i knew it might happen but i wasnt quite ready for it to happen when i had seen him pull up i said here here it goes and he just popped in the door i dont know exactly what it was but something i sort of think of it as a reserve energy
Response: it sounds like you anticipated something happening but were not entirely prepared for it in that moment you tapped into a reserve energy to help you cope with the situation can you tell me more about how you felt in that moment and how the reserve energy helped you

Context: ive been feeling completely depleted lately but somehow ive been able to pull from this backup energy source i experienced a whole range of emotions and even though i came out shaky i felt proud that i stood up and did what needed to be done
Response: its great to hear that youve been able to find a backup energy source during difficult times but its also important to address the root cause of your depletion what situations or factors might be contributing to this feeling of emptiness once we identify these factors we can work together to develop strategies for better selfcare and stress management

Context: i didnt let her get away with it even though i was new to the social situation i think it took some courage for me to stand up
Response: it sounds like you were the first person to really stand up in that situation and as a new person it must have taken a lot of guts im impressed by your courage and i think you should be proud of yourself for taking action

Context: sometimes i dont praise myself but ive not given much thought to it over the weekend i thought about a recent event and i didnt think about having to see the person involved again on tuesday on monday when i saw the appointment in my book i got a rush and realized im going to have to face this situation again
Response: its important to acknowledge and praise yourself for your achievements and improvements reflecting on past events can help you grow and learn from them its also normal to feel anxious about facing a difficult situation or meeting with someone you had an issue with try to identify what makes you uncomfortable in this situation and take small steps to address it remember facing these challenges with a positive attitude can help you in building better relationships and personal growth

Context: ive been constantly telling myself that i can do this and that im on the right track ive learned from my mistakes and ive taken appropriate measures to improve i went in and said my piece
Response: its great to hear that youre working on building your selfconfidence and working towards improvement positive selftalk can be beneficial for personal growth be sure to also forgive yourself for past mistakes when moving forward and remember that its okay to seek additional support if needed is there anything in particular that is still causing you worry or concern

Context: i had a conversation with someone recently and she argued with me but it wasnt like the previous week the tone was more civilized this time and she disagreed with how i handled the situation i also expressed my thoughts on the matter
Response: its good to hear that the communication was more civilized compared to the previous week it seems like you both are attempting to express your opinions and resolve the issue can you tell me more about the situation you were discussing and the ways both of you have handled it so far

Context: im angry about my sister making a farce out of returning and my brotherinlaw treating her badly last week i felt so much love for her but now i feel disappointed shes not in the household anymore i still care for her but im just so angry what kind of a moron does something like that
Response: its understandable that youre angry about how your sister was treated and that she is no longer in the household however its important to remember that you still care for her and thats what matters most people make mistakes and can act like morons but that doesnt mean you should stop loving them try to focus on the love you have for her and be there to support her in this difficult time

Context: i dont love interacting with people who i consider to be foolish or less intelligent because of this i prefer to stay inside and avoid socializing with others i feel disappointed about this aspect of myself and this has been an ongoing issue for me
Response: it seems like you have strong feelings about avoiding people who you perceive as less intelligent ultimately leading to isolation and disappointment within yourself this issue appears to be affecting your personal relationships and social life you mentioned this has been a continuing problem can you share more about the impact this behavior has on your life or any specific events that triggered these feelings

Context: i dont even know what i am now im just me and this is the way i was born you know i dont like people very much and they never fail to fulfill my expectations of their jerkiness i want to go im done i want to go right now
Response: you were born not liking people its important for us to talk to each other through trouble not by getting alienated during trouble i understand you may want to leave but i think its crucial that we stay together to work on this issue lets try to identify the origin of your dislike for people and find a better way to cope with your feelings

Context: recently i have realized that theres a darker side to me that is always present i am not interested in anyone including myself and i am unable to see any potential improvement right now
Response: its important to acknowledge and explore all aspects of oneself including the darker side however its also crucial not to lose hope or give up on yourself can you tell me more about what specifically is making you feel this way lets find ways to address it and create a better balance in your life

Context: im really not sure just who i am i mean when it comes right down to it you ask me who that is thats above the dork or hipster or whatever you wanna call it but i dont know who that is i dont know who i am whats the overriding i
Response: its completely normal to feel unsure about your identity at times instead of focusing on labels like dork or hipster try to think about the qualities interests and values that make you unique its important not to get too caught up in these labels as they can be limiting remember selfdiscovery is a lifelong process and who you are may change and evolve over time can you tell me about some of your interests and values that might give us a better understanding of who you are

Context: lately ive been struggling to figure out who my real self is and its causing me to feel constantly conflicted in different situations for example ive been experiencing interpersonal conflicts and arguments even over simple things like at the supermarket and it seems like its become my way of life
Response: it sounds like youre experiencing some internal conflicts and thats being projected outwardly through the interpersonal conflicts youre having its important to understand that we all have different aspects of ourselves depending on the context and situation instead of trying to pinpoint one real self focus on embracing the different parts of yourself and finding a healthy balance remember not all conflicts are harmful some can lead to invigorating conversations or personal growth if youre constantly worrying about this perhaps we could explore these conflicts together and work on embracing the various parts of your personality

Context: as a patient im struggling with an internal conflict between two aspects of myself the dork and the hip person i feel like theres a voice inside me saying youre not good enough im not sure how to relate to the world outside and resolve conflicts with other people
Response: as a counsellor i understand youre experiencing an internal conflict between the dork and the hip person aspects of yourself as well as feeling pressure from a voice saying youre not good enough its essential to explore the perspectives of both the dork and the hip person and what they would say to each other this way you can understand their roles in your life and create a healthier balance which may help you better relate to the world outside and resolve conflicts with others

Context: i dont know what theyd say but i know they wouldnt like each other
Response: it seems like youre uncertain about how these individuals would interact and express their dislike for each other considering that you dont have specific information it might be helpful to step back and acknowledge that you cannot control or predict others actions or behavior focus on what you can control such as your own reactions and interactions with others

Context: ive always thought of myself as a dork and i tend to ignore this side of myself because i find it unattractive and useless however i am starting to realize that maybe ignoring this part of me could be limiting my vitality and versatility
Response: its important to acknowledge and accept all parts of ourselves even those we might perceive as unattractive or useless by embracing these aspects we can actually tap into our full potential and enrich our lives with increased vitality and versatility so dont hide or suppress your dorky side  instead try to find ways to express and appreciate it remember every aspect of your personality contributes to making you a unique individual

Context: i feel like i have this gap between my dork side and my hip side and im not sure how to bring them together i dont want to be a dork because im scared of people and feel insecure about myself
Response: its okay to feel a gap between different aspects of your personality instead of completely rejecting your dork side lets first understand it and what it brings to your life its important to embrace all parts of yourself as this can lead to a more authentic and balanced sense of self can you share what qualities you appreciate about your hip side

Context: im having trouble with the dork and hipster sides of myself and i dont want that dork in me im wondering how the dork could take what the hipster offers and what the hipster could contribute to the dork
Response: it sounds like youre experiencing some internal conflicts between different aspects of yourself instead of seeing the dork and the hipster as separate and incompatible consider how they can learn from each other and contribute positively to your overall self they can coexist and balance each other out allowing you to show various facets of your personality when needed what positive qualities do you think each aspect can bring to the other

Context: im not comfortable with this hip thing i dont think im a hip guy and i have trouble tolerating the excitement of the idea positive thoughts about myself and the idea of my inner complexity do not sit easily within my mind
Response: its completely normal to feel uncomfortable with certain aspects of ourselves its important to remember that selfacceptance is a journey its okay to question and explore different parts of your personality i would encourage you to try embracing your strengths and acknowledging your limitations without being too hard on yourself it might help you achieve a better sense of selfunderstanding

Context: im disappointed that i couldnt help my sister it doesnt hurt me though because its not my problem we lived together for eight days but it was just like staying with her when we were 17
Response: it seems like youre feeling disappointed about the situation with your sister but youre distancing yourself from the issue because its her problem its important to note that its possible for situations to affect both people involved do you think there might be some romanticism or hidden emotions in your perspective

Context: i dont like the romantic side of myself and i dont expect great things for my sister as it seems like an idealized fantasy i feel like im in a bad way
Response: i understand that you feel conflicted about your romantic side and you dont want to have unrealistic expectations for your sister its okay to feel this way and its important to recognize your feelings can you share more about why you view these expectations as a fantasy and how it affects your relationship with your sister

Context: i have a sense that most things are vaguely boring at least vaguely boring and mundane there are real problems and i see that there are problems but it seems like i have forgotten how to want something
Response: it sounds like you are experiencing a lack of motivation and feeling like life has lost its excitement its important to recognize that its normal to feel this way at times but we can work towards reigniting your passions and desires can you think of any past experiences or activities that used to bring you joy or excitement

Context: i dont do anything exceptional i write lame ad copy for local stuff and the expectations are not high its all in the southern california area so its not a big deal this session is actually boring me
Response: i understand that you may feel unfulfilled or unchallenged in your work as the expectations are not high and its local to southern california its completely normal to experience dissatisfaction if your job doesnt challenge you or help you grow can you think of any aspects of your work that you enjoy or any possible changes you could make to your role to make it more rewarding

Context: i attended a session with my counsellor and while they found our first session illuminating and exciting i didnt share the same feeling they tried to resonate with me using provocative language thinking it would help engage me since i have an irreverent and rebellious attitude but it didnt make the session exciting for me
Response: as your counsellor i apologize if my previous approach didnt work well for you i was trying to connect with you by resonating with your presumed attitude but its clear that it didnt have the desired effect moving forward lets discuss what kind of approach you would prefer in our sessions to help me better understand and support you your feedback is important to make this a productive experience for both of us

Context: i have a habit of keeping people including my counsellor at a distance i dont think i want to keep them out but its just something i do
Response: it seems like you recognize this pattern of distancing yourself from others and it could be something youve developed for various reasons like protecting yourself emotionally as your counsellor im willing to work with you at your pace to better understand why this habit has formed and together we can explore strategies to foster more comfortable open relationships is there any particular situation or relationship where youve seen this distancing affect you most

Context: i had told her what i was gonna be wearing and described myself however i didnt mention that i would be dishevelled i was extremely selfconscious
Response: its quite normal to feel selfconscious in such situations especially when meeting someone new in the future you can choose to be more open about your appearance to avoid any misunderstandings or anxiety is there anything in particular about your appearance that makes you feel selfconscious

Context: i have been noticing and worrying about where my hands should be like if they should be here there or in another specific position
Response: it seems like you are overly conscious about the position of your hands which could be a sign of anxiety or selfconsciousness can you tell me if there are any specific situations where you feel this way so we can better understand and address your concern

Context: i was concentrating on myself during the conversation and i had this internal dialogue where i kept telling myself to say something intelligent but then i would just respond back to myself saying that i had nothing to say it was incredibly distracting
Response: it sounds like you were putting a lot of pressure on yourself to perform in the conversation which can be quite distracting keep in mind that its normal to have an internal dialogue but try not to let it overwhelm you instead of focusing on saying something intelligent just focus on being present and engaged in the conversation remember its okay to take a moment to gather your thoughts before responding

Context: i was trying to have a conversation with someone but i didnt want to make banal chatter i tried to say something witty but we ended up talking about computers  which is a topic that i am familiar with it was a dull conversation and im feeling disappointed with myself for not making it more interesting
Response: its understandable that you wanted to have a more engaging conversation but its okay that it didnt turn out as you expected dont be too hard on yourself  sometimes people have dull conversations and its not a reflection of your wit or ability to connect with others instead of focusing on this one experience consider it a learning opportunity and think about ways to improve future interactions if youre comfortable sharing can you let me know more about why you felt the need to say something witty

Context: i recently had a conversation with someone and it seemed a little tense at first we both seemed to loosen up a bit by the end of the conversation i tried asking her out on friday but she said she was busy i took that as a no and im not sure how to interpret her response
Response: its understandable that you might be feeling uncertain about her response its possible that she was genuinely busy on friday or she might not be interested in going out with you its important to respect her schedule and boundaries however since you said the conversation was getting better towards the end you can consider asking her if theres another day that works for her this way you can gauge her interest while being respectful of her time

Context: i think gerald knows himself pretty well but he misunderstands his possibilities or has given up on his needs and desires i havent left my house for 90 days and im not pleased with it but im uncomfortable around people i have everything i need and have a social life
Response: thank you for sharing your feelings gerald it seems like you are trying to cope with your discomfort around people by staying at home while it may provide some peace there might be other ways to address this discomfort to improve your opportunities to fulfill your needs and desires can you please tell me more about your social life and activities you enjoy doing

Context: i have an electronic social life and a girlfriend in toronto but the thing is i dont really know what she is and she doesnt know what i am i dont even know if its a woman and thats the weird thing about having a social life thats electronic
Response: it sounds like you are in a unique situation where you have a relationship with someone online but theres uncertainty about their identity its normal to have concerns in situations like these can you tell me more about how this uncertainty affects your feelings and thoughts about the relationship

Context: i am six foot two and im confused about the satisfaction we get from our social life im out of the house right now but i wonder whats the big deal with it
Response: it seems like you are questioning the importance and satisfaction derived from social life social interactions can be essential for our mental wellbeing as they provide a sense of belonging support and opportunities to connect with others my question to you is do you feel satisfied with your current social life and does this affect your overall life satisfaction

Context: i feel like when i say something it doesnt matter much to the other person they easily ride over my words and it seems like they have their mind made up i tried to express my thoughts but they didnt let me finish
Response: i understand that it must be frustrating to feel unheard and disregarded as a counsellor its essential to ensure that both parties are equally engaged in the conversation can you give more details on the context of the conversation and how it affects your emotional wellbeing

Context: ive never really tried to be kind but in a big emergency im able to put aside my misanthropy and help out
Response: well kindness doesnt always require effort it can be natural id like to know a specific instance when youve been kind whether it was intentional or not instead of generalizing lets focus on one particular moment of kindness you have experienced

Context: when i was in high school i had to work during the summer to help my mothers struggling business while my friends enjoyed their vacation at marthas vineyard it was an emergency situation and i did it out of kindness for someone close to me
Response: it sounds like you made a selfless decision to help your mother during a difficult time instead of indulging in the leisure activities like your friends it must have been tough to make that sacrifice but it shows your strong sense of responsibility and love for your mother can you share how this experience might have shaped your perspectives or values later in life

Context: ive been struggling with focusing on the present moment i tend to skip ahead in conversations but this time i caught myself and shared it instead of keeping it to myself
Response: its great that youre becoming more aware of your tendency to skip ahead and acknowledging it this shows progress in developing mindfulness and selfawareness keep practicing and try to fully engage in the present moment remember its okay to catch yourself and share your experience with others

Context: ive been skipping ahead in life and recently realized that it would be nice to deal with people on another level its a new thought and i wonder who could put up with me for three hours
Response: its great that youve recognized the desire to connect with people on a deeper level as your counsellor im here to help you work through your thoughts and feelings even if it might take more than one session dont worry about the time it takes the focus should be on your growth and understanding how to build stronger connections with others

Context: ive been in therapy before and im not really convinced about the idea of insight leading to change my sister a therapist convinced me to come here but im not fully on board with this process im not an idiot and i dont have a lot of faith in therapy
Response: i understand your skepticism and feelings about therapy and its okay to express your doubts its important to remember that each therapy experience can be different and some approaches may work better for you than others would you be open to discuss what aspects of therapy were unhelpful for you in the past and if theres a different approach we can explore

Context: i think a lot of people are really stupid and boring and i know im not an idiot but i dont do well with my social interactions my office went virtual and i do everything by computer my wife doesnt see that theres no difference since there are no physical office gettogethers anymore
Response: it sounds like you are struggling with social interactions and are feeling misunderstood by your wife its important to acknowledge that virtual environments can impact social connections differently have you tried discussing these changes with your wife and possibly finding alternative ways to interact with others to improve your social experiences

Context: recently i had a fun date which went as expected but still left me feeling angry and overall bad
Response: its interesting that you felt angry and bad after your fun date even though it went as expected can you tell me more about what specifically triggered these negative emotions it would be helpful to understand the situation better and offer guidance on how to cope with such emotions in the future

Context: i was recently told by someone that i appeared disheveled and even though they mentioned other things as well i cant seem to get past that term im unsure if i really looked disheveled but the fact that they thought so bothers me
Response: i understand that being called disheveled might have affected you negatively its natural to feel hurt or judged when someone makes a comment about your appearance however try focusing on why this particular comment has stuck with you and whether there is an underlying concern or insecurity if you feel the need you can share with me the other things this person said to better understand the context of that conversation

Context: i recently had an interaction with someone who was very bright and it went really badly i wasnt smooth at all and it was exactly what i had predicted
Response: i understand that the interaction didnt go as youd hoped and it can be frustrating when things dont go smoothly can you provide more details about what specifically happened during the interaction so we can better analyze the situation and find ways to improve your communication skills

Context: i went on a date with someone i liked but i didnt have funny things to say or intelligent banter to engage her with at the end of the date i asked her if she wanted to go out again but she declined surprisingly im not as miserable about it as i thought id be
Response: its good to hear that youre not feeling too miserable about the outcome of the date rejection can be hard to handle but its important to remember that not every person we meet will be a perfect match instead of focusing on the lack of connection try to learn from this experience and consider how you might improve your communication skills or find more common ground in future dates can you tell me more about what happened during the date so we have a clearer picture of the situation

Context: i dont want to hurt other people for no reason is that a positive thing or just a personality default
Response: as a counsellor its important to note that not wanting to hurt others is generally a positive thing as it demonstrates empathy and consideration for others feelings its not necessarily a personality default id like to know more about why you consider this trait to be potentially negative could you please elaborate on that concern

Context: i feel like there are two sides of me one side has moments when i could hurt someone for no reason but i choose not to i often think about whether its kind not to run over a puppy in the road
Response: its normal for people to feel like they have different aspects of their personality in your case it seems that youre trying to navigate between your aggressive impulses and your compassionate side instead of focusing on whether not running over a puppy is considered kind try to evaluate your actions based on their overall impact on others and your own personal values

Context: i want to bring my good side into the light of day but i cant see the kind side of me and i feel dominated and defeated
Response: it can be challenging to recognize your own positive qualities when feeling dominated or defeated lets focus on what you can do to genuinely express your kindness are there any specific situations or people where youve shown kindness in the past reflecting on those experiences might help you see the kind side of yourself

Context: i feel like theres something wrong but i cant quite put my finger on it you make it seem like its something that we can talk about but i dont see it i cant say ive never been kind but im just not sure what the issue is
Response: i understand that youre feeling confused about what might be troubling you sometimes it can be challenging to identify the root cause of our discomfort im here to help you explore your thoughts and feelings can you think of any specific situation or emotion that bothers you or that youd like to discuss further

Context: i got in trouble when i was eleven years old the principal called me in and threatened me and said that he would suspend me next time its not real trouble i mean they dont do anything to eleven year olds also i was treated very badly by two therapists but it doesnt really matter
Response: its interesting that you mention the trouble you had with the principal when you were eleven and then the poor treatment you received from the therapists but you also say it doesnt matter there seems to be a contradiction in how you perceive these events on one hand you describe them as terrible yet on the other you downplay their significance can you help me understand why you feel this way about these experiences

Context: im feeling upset because my friend told my principal that i was smoking when i was eleven i think it was terrible of him to do that also i want to mention that i consider myself a very analytical person and i believe that i have insight into myself
Response: i understand why you might feel betrayed by your friend for telling the principal its important to differentiate between the two issues the smoking itself and your friends choice to share that information as an analytical person you might want to consider why your friend felt the need to tell your principal and how it affects your relationship remember that no ones selfinsight is perfect so its essential to remain open to new perspectives and growth is there any particular reason you wanted to share this incident with me

Context: i felt mildly offended when the counsellor made a confrontation because they didnt want me to set the boundaries of what i can and cant learn from our sessions together i felt amused by their comment that they got through to me
Response: as a counsellor i apologize if my statement was offensive my intention was to challenge the boundaries and encourage open communication during our sessions its important to address any discomfort or frustration so we can work together to explore and address your concerns effectively can you share more on why you felt offended and what specific boundaries you would like to maintain

Context: i feel like i always have to do everything by myself and im struggling with the isolation that it brings i end up interrupting others because im always in my own world
Response: i understand that you feel isolated and the struggle that comes with it its important to work on allowing others to be a part of your life and coordinating with them to ease that feeling can you think of any situations where you can make an effort to let others in and work together on a task

Context: i feel like this is therapy and i should be telling you about myself but im unsure what to talk about
Response: thats completely normal in therapy we do focus on you so lets begin by discussing your habits of mind what influences your thoughts actions and how you perceive situations this way we can better understand what you go through on a daily basis and explore what might be causing any distress in your life

Context: i had bad therapists before and they broke confidentiality when i talked to suzanne about my issues i feel like my reflexes were established a long time ago and have nothing to do with whats going on now
Response: it sounds like youve had some negative experiences with therapists in the past and its understandable that you might be hesitant to trust in the process now as a counsellor i would like to assure you that maintaining confidentiality is a priority for me in order to help you id like to know which specific aspects of your past therapy you found unhelpful and how they might be impacting your current situation

Context: i recently had a bad experience when someone told my principal about something i said in therapy
Response: i understand that it must be frustrating to have your privacy invaded like that can you please elaborate on what exactly happened and how it has affected you this would help me in providing better guidance and support for your situation

Context: i took her attitude as a no i took her no as a no it was a clear no her attitude was no not ever
Response: as a counsellor i understand that youre interpreting her response in a very absolute manner however its important to consider that peoples feelings and thoughts can change over time instead of focusing solely on this rejection try to be more open to understanding her perspective and remember that no is not necessarily forever is there any specific situation or incident that triggered this feeling of rejection

Context: as the patient i recently had a conversation with my counsellor where i expressed my perspective on a situation i admitted that i understand why my counsellor cant trust my judgments because of the way i make them i suggested that my counsellor should call someone else to get a clearer understanding
Response: as the counsellor i acknowledge your awareness of the issue and understand the reason for your suggestion i appreciate your honesty and the growth youve made in recognizing your thought patterns instead of focusing on mistrust lets work together on improving your judgmentmaking abilities and develop a stronger trust in yourself and your perceptions

Context: ive been told that my humor is sharp and quick and my language is metaphorical and colorful ive accepted this recognition of my positive qualities for the first time however i dont know what to do about it and i worry that insight doesnt lead to change
Response: its great that youve accepted the recognition of your positive qualities and your concern about implementing change is understandable change may not be instant but insight can be a starting point you can take one step at a time reflect on your thoughts and actions and gradually integrate your unique qualities into daily life in a balanced and effective manner dont be too hard on yourself change takes time and patience

Context: i dont take compliments well i dont like compliments i dont like to be complimented why do you think that is
Response: ah the reason i think it is is because youre not going to like this but im gonna tell you the answer to your question anyway its likely that you have issues with selfesteem or selfworth which make it difficult for you to accept compliments you might feel that you dont deserve the praise or you might be uncomfortable with the attention it brings its important to work on building your selfconfidence and accepting compliments as a healthy part of social interactions

Context: ive been trying to get out of the house every day because i think its good for me when i go outside the air feels nice and it feels good to be out of the house
Response: its great that you are making an effort to get out of the house daily as it can indeed be beneficial for your mental health how do you typically spend your time when youre outdoors

Context: i feel like ive gotten something out of this therapy and i like that you dont take any nonsense from me however ive been thinking about stopping this therapy since i have a social life now what do you think about it
Response: i believe its important not to view therapy as an on or off situation but i understand if you want it to be like that i would like to remind you of your power to work through barriers and not completely disregard therapy if a problem arises in the future leaving the option openended might be beneficial

Context: im not sure if we should continue our therapy sessions or not and if we do what would be the best way to do it should we decrease the frequency of our meetings
Response: as a counsellor i believe that therapy isnt an on or off thing but rather an availability when you need it we could consider tapering off and scheduling sessions less frequently such as once a month that way youll still have access to help whenever needed while adjusting to a less frequent schedule

Context: i think it would be a good idea to see each other once a month for a few months to gradually stop our sessions we can then evaluate how things go and decide whats best for me
Response: that sounds like a reasonable plan we can schedule monthly sessions to help in your transition monitor your progress and address any concerns you might have ensuring that you feel comfortable and confident in managing on your own is our main priority lets move forward with this plan and assess its effectiveness as we go

Context: i never used to be visibly uncomfortable but this time i couldnt muster the yes bob thats a good idea and i was having troubles with it i feel like im unable to go out and interact with humans
Response: it sounds like youre experiencing a change in your ability to interact and navigate social situations comfortably could there be something specific that happened recently that triggered this change in you remember its completely normal to have ups and downs and finding the root cause can help you address and work through this situation

Context: i feel like im becoming unable to do something that i used to do and its really disturbing and immobilizing
Response: i understand how distressing and immobilizing this can be for you i would like to help you address this issue if youre willing to share more information could you please explain the situation or task that youre struggling with

Context: i shared my thoughts with bob about the campaign being wrong on a couple of accounts and i didnt like the slogan i suggested that if we came up with a better idea the giveaway would be moot and people would be interested in the product already however bobs reaction was simply this is my idea
Response: it seems like you expressed your disagreement with bobs campaign idea and offered an alternative viewpoint aiming at a better outcome however it appears that bob responded defensively without acknowledging your concerns as a counsellor i suggest exploring the reasons behind your disagreement and try to approach bob in a more collaborative way to find common ground how has your working relationship with bob been before this interaction

Context: i recently overheard my coworker talking to my boss and saying i think its a damn good idea i dont know the exact details of their conversation but i feel anxious and unsure about what they were discussing it makes me feel like im always several steps behind and maybe i should be moving faster
Response: its understandable to feel worried about feeling left out of important conversations at work however its important not to jump to conclusions about what they were discussing without any concrete information instead try to focus on your own tasks and keep an open line of communication with your boss and coworkers if theres something you need to be aware of or involved in trust that they will include you when necessary

Context: im not happy with this session i feel like ive been caught in a lie and ive never thought i was unable to be caught i can see some sense in what youre saying but i dont like this situation
Response: i understand that being caught in a lie can be uncomfortable its important to acknowledge when we make mistakes or feel vulnerable its a learning experience for both of us even though you didnt like this session it might have been important for your growth are there any specific aspects of the session that bothered you

Context: i went to a party this week and it was kind of an interesting experience im thinking of becoming a party boy

Context: ive been working really hard lately changing ducts in my friends attic and taking care of my kids i have this vivid imagination of mowing the lawn with my one and a half year old in a snugly my 3yearold in a back carrier and my other child by the window where i can see her
Response: it sounds like you have a lot on your plate managing both work and your childrens care this can be quite overwhelming and tiring dont hesitate to reach out to friends family or support networks to help you in balancing these responsibilities its essential to take the time for yourself too to relax and manage your stress levels is there a specific concern thats bothering you more

Context: i used to be very trustworthy and kept my word but over the last six months ive felt discriminated against and its affecting my online interactions and confidence in myself ive never felt this kind of selfdoubt before
Response: its important to recognize that your sense of selfworth is being affected by these experiences its possible that the online environment may not be the best for you but the main concern is regaining your confidence i encourage you to reflect on your strengths and work on rebuilding your selfesteem whether you decide to stay online or engage with others offline stay true to your values as a trustworthy person and focus on how to overcome this selfdoubt

Context: at florida state university i was in the snare line for four years in high school our school had a top football team and our marching band was pretty good too i thought i became better by being in the marching band
Response: its great to hear that being in the marching band had a positive impact on you during your time at florida state university its important to recognize and celebrate our achievements can you think of any specific ways that being part of the marching band has helped you grow or learn new skills

Context: i dont want my kids to suffer at all and i dont want them to have any troubles but life just seems to hand us troubles i tried to protect them but it didnt work
Response: its natural for a parent to want to protect their children from any harm or struggles however life does present challenges and its important to remember that facing these difficulties can lead to growth and character development just like in your own personal experiences while it may not have gone as planned it seems that these experiences have brought you and your children closer together in some ways which can be a positive outcome its important to focus on supporting them and helping them navigate through the challenges life presents

Context: ive been feeling down lately and struggling with selfcriticism its affecting my relationships and i often feel like nobody wants me i came to you for help and you suggested an assignment for me to go to the shopping mall or airport observe people in relationships and try to realize that there are people with flaws who are still loved
Response: im glad you completed the assignment and shared your observations with me its important to understand that everyone has imperfections yet this doesnt prevent them from being in loving relationships selfcriticism can be damaging so remind yourself of your own value and know that someone will love you for who you are focus on selfimprovement and selflove to build confidence in yourself and your relationships do you feel any different after completing this assignment

Context: when i was younger my father who was a psychologist and i used to make monthly trips to the store together he was financially welloff and we lived at a nice beach house during these trips we would always get three things  a paperback book for my father a sirloin steak from the butcher and breyers ice cream
Response: thank you for sharing this story about your father it helps me better understand your background and relationship with him it sounds like these trips to the store were special bonding moments between you two is there a particular lesson or piece of advice from your father that has stayed with you throughout the years that you believe would be relevant to the topic of our discussion

Context: i adored my father more than anyone in the world but he would sometimes do things that would rub me the wrong way i think he was trying to teach me to love someone immensely in spite of their mistakes but i still havent mastered it what advice would my father give me now if he were here given what weve discussed about my life and current frustrations
Response: it seems your father was trying to teach you an important lesson about love and acceptance if he were here now he might say to focus on the love and connection you shared and remember that everyone makes mistakes instead of dwelling on the frustrations try to practice empathy and understanding in your relationships is there a specific situation or relationship that youre struggling with right now where you can apply this lesson

Context: when i think about what someone might advise me at this point i think they would say do what youve always done in this situation that means i should trust myself
Response: its great that you have received advice to trust yourself as selftrust can be an essential aspect of personal growth and decisionmaking in this context can you give me an example of a similar situation where youve trusted yourself and it helped you to make the right choice

Context: i notice that i havent planned to be centered while doing my thing but i think it should just happen naturally im also realizing that getting out of the office and doing many things is essential for my projects
Response: its great to acknowledge the importance of being centered and getting out of the office for your projects being centered can positively impact your overall wellbeing and productivity when youre more present and mindful youre likely to create better connections with others and discover new opportunities being open to new experiences and stepping outside of your comfort zone can lead to personal growth and a more fulfilling life remember its about finding a balance and allowing yourself to be present in your daily activities

Context: im in a situation where the things at home seem to affect my mood and im not sure how to handle it i guess i need to explore the world more and let someone see the real me this strategy has worked before but im kind of nervous about it
Response: its understandable that you feel nervous about stepping out of your comfort zone based on your past success with this strategy its worth considering trying it again dont completely abandon your current coping mechanisms but supplement them with new experiences and connections this may provide you with a better perspective on your situation and potentially help you feel happier and more focused

Context: ive been working hard and distracting myself after recovering from a difficult time i feel like im in a good place relationshipwise now but i still struggle with the effects of what my kids have been through
Response: its good to hear that you have made progress in your personal life its natural to worry about the impact of past difficulties on your children have you considered seeking professional help for your kids to address any lingering issues they might be facing

Context: i find it difficult to handle the troubles my kids go through in life like being bullied heartbreak or the way my marital troubles might be influencing them it saddens me but i understand that these experiences shape them as individuals
Response: its normal to feel concerned about your childrens wellbeing but youre right that these experiences contribute to their personal growth as dr erickson mentioned we can consider the troubles of life as roughage an essential part of our development remember you can provide support and guidance for your kids but its also important to let them learn and grow from their experiences if theres a specific worry thats been bothering you lately feel free to share it with me

Context: i want you to help me become more relaxed yes i dont want to be so defensive with you i dont like to feel so defensive
Response: its great to acknowledge that one way to help you feel more relaxed and less defensive is by practicing open communication lets try expressing your feelings or thoughts whenever you feel defensive so we can better understand each other and work towards making you feel comfortable

Context: as a patient i am feeling quite upset because i was called a phony by someone for smiling when im embarrassed or put in a corner i admit that i find it hard to show my embarrassment but i dont think its fair to call me a phony
Response: as a counsellor i acknowledge your feelings and understand that being called a phony can be hurtful its important to remember that everyone has different ways of dealing with embarrassment and smiling may be your coping mechanism it doesnt necessarily mean youre being insincere focus on expressing your true feelings and try not to worry too much about others judgments in what other situations do you find yourself feeling embarrassed

Context: i feel like youre picking on me and i want to pick on you too however i have to wait until you say something that i can pick on im struggling to find words for my feelings and i wish i could start our interaction all over again
Response: i apologize if it feels like im picking on you thats not my intention its helpful to know how youre experiencing our conversation lets take a moment to start fresh and focus on your feelings if you could express your feelings through a movement or action what would that be like for you

Context: im scared and suspicious of you i think you understand that when i get scared i laugh or kid to cover up im afraid of your direct attack and want you to be more on my side i feel like going back to a corner where im completely protected
Response: it sounds like youre feeling scared and vulnerable and using laughter as a way to cope i want to assure you that my intention is to support and help you not to attack you can you tell me more about the corner youd like to be in where you feel completely protected

Context: i know i wouldnt really feel safe but being in a corner feels safer for me this reminds me of when i was a little girl and every time i was afraid id feel better sitting in a corner but panicky
Response: it sounds like youre experiencing a similar feeling of safety in a corner as you did when you were a child its important to recognize that you are not a little girl anymore but im wondering if the corner provides a sense of comfort due to its familiarity can you think of ways to create a sense of safety and comfort in other situations without relying on a corner

Context: i am a 30 year old woman and i feel afraid of you i become really defensive in this situation i dont know why it reminds me of something
Response: its important to recognize that youre feeling afraid and defensive however im here to support you and help you work through any issues you are facing it is natural to feel vulnerable in a counselling environment can you share more about what this feeling reminds you of it might help us to understand the underlying emotions or past experiences that are causing this fear

Context: i feel so dumb and stupid because i dont have the right answers this makes me feel inferior to others like i have to look up to them because theyre smarter
Response: its quite common to compare ourselves with others and feel inadequate at times however constantly feeling inferior is not healthy remember that everyone has their strengths and weaknesses and having all the right answers is not a measure of ones worth its essential to focus on personal growth and selfacceptance is there a specific situation where you felt this way recently

Context: i had a feeling i could be afraid of you as you seem like someone who demands a lot of respect i think my fear has to do with my father but i dont feel like i demand respect personally
Response: it appears that you have a desire for more respect from others which may be rooted in your relationship with your father can you think of any specific instances in your life where you felt disrespected and how it affected you

Context: i feel that if i put myself in a vulnerable position you wont help me at all i cant seem to live up to your expectations and i tend to wait in my safe corner until someone comes to rescue me
Response: it seems like you rely on others to rescue you from difficult situations and you feel im not supportive if you find yourself in a tight spot wouldnt it be more empowering to muster the courage to get out on your own rather than expecting someone else to always pull you out

Context: i feel like youre calling me phony for admitting my vulnerabilities and waiting for someone to help me im being honest about my situation and resent being judged for it i think im just as real sitting in that corner as i am standing on my own
Response: i apologize if my earlier statement made you feel judged its important to recognize and understand our vulnerabilities however i want to encourage you to find your own strength and not solely rely on others for your growth remember its okay to ask for help but finding a balance between selfreliance and support is crucial for personal development

Context: i feel like you dont like me right off the bat and i want to know if you do i think youd say that im a phony flip little girl and a show off
Response: as a counsellor my aim is to help you not judge you its important to focus on your feelings and thoughts rather than trying to guess what i think its natural to feel insecure or defensive but lets work together to explore your thoughts and emotions without making assumptions about each other can you tell me more about why you feel the need to label yourself as a phony

Context: i feel like youre showing off and acting like you know all the answers it makes you seem less human to me like youre trying to find a reason for every little action i take
Response: i apologize if it seems that way i have observed some of your actions but i am not claiming to know all the answers as a counsellor its my job to observe and understand your behavior if you feel uncomfortable please let me know how i can better support you

Context: i want you to acknowledge and accept my physical behaviors like kicking my feet and giggling when im nervous without putting me on the defensive i dont want to have to explain why im doing these things
Response: i understand your concern i didnt actually ask you to explain your behavior but rather just observed what you were doing its important to separate my observations from your interpretation or imagination please continue expressing yourself and remember that im here to support and help you

Context: i dont think im playing stupid but the counsellor seems to suggest otherwise i just did something with my hair during our conversation and he asked if there was something in his hair that i object to but theres nothing
Response: thank you for sharing your thoughts it seems like there could be a misunderstanding between you and the counsellor regarding the comment about playing stupid as a counsellor it is important for me to understand your actions and expressions better  so could you kindly provide more context or explain what you meant by doing something with your hair

Context: as the patient i feel like we found some closure and understanding during our conversation it seems like a good point to end the session
Response: as the counsellor i agree with you that we have reached a nice closure and gained some understanding in this session it is indeed a good point to wrap up our conversation remember you can always reach out if you need further assistance take care and be well

Context: as a patient i feel like youre judgmental and i dont feel close to you at all i think youve never felt the way i feel and you just pass judgment on people like me it seems like youre playing a game and lack genuine feelings
Response: as a counsellor i understand that you feel this way and i apologize if my behavior came across as judgmental my intention is to help you not to belittle or hurt your feelings though our conversation may involve some games my ultimate goal is to support you and make a meaningful connection i want you to feel comfortable and understood can you please share more about why you feel im being judgmental so i can improve my approach

Context: i cant help but feel irritated with people who act cocksure and smart like they have all the answers id like to embarrass them and show them that they can be just as phony as anyone else theres this person who looks distinguished and i feel like its just another advantage they have
Response: it seems like youre frustrated with people who appear overconfident and selfassured and you desire to bring them down a notch the distinguished appearance of this person could be adding to your irritation what elements of their behavior or attitude bother you the most reflecting on this may help you better understand your feelings and develop a healthier response to their actions

Context: i feel like youre not recognizing me at all dr perls and it makes me mad you seem so detached and you dont even seem to care that im upset with you i feel like im not being heard
Response: i apologize if it seems like im not recognizing your feelings my intent is not to ignore your emotions but to create a safe space for open communication i appreciate you sharing your anger with me and your concerns about my detachment can you tell me more about why you feel im not recognizing you so i can better understand and address your concerns

Context: i feel nervous about driving on my own and i worry that i might panic and have to pull over but talking about it and practicing breathing exercises make me feel more confident
Response: its great that youre practicing breathing exercises and gaining confidence through talking about your concerns if you do feel panicked while driving remember to breathe and remind yourself that its just your heart racing  you can do this lets go over your selfdialogue and practice visualizing yourself successfully managing your nervousness

Context: i get really anxious while driving especially by the bank im afraid that i might panic lose control and possibly cause an accident ive been working on some coping strategies but im still quite worried
Response: its great that youve been working on coping strategies based on what youve learned it seems like panicking isnt likely to happen and even if it does it wont overwhelm you to manage your feelings while driving you can stay focused use your breathing to relax remind yourself that its just your heart beating faster and remember that the anxiety will go away once you get through the situation if you need to you can always pull over and calm down before starting again would you like to modify any of these strategies or add anything else that might help you feel stronger

Context: i have been experiencing nightmares and sweating and i avoid thinking of the traumatic event i had my husband suggested i seek help can my condition be treated
Response: yes it seems like youre experiencing ptsd and seeking counseling is a big step towards overcoming it there are effective approaches to treat ptsd that have worked for many people we can discuss your options and i will also give you a book explaining more about ptsd and its treatment we can start by talking about your incident in more detail but you can choose what you want to share how does that sound to you

Context: im feeling a bit nervous my anxiety is about a three or four i might need to take a break if i get too overwhelmed but ill try to remind myself of the positive selfstatements ive learned
Response: absolutely its important to take breaks and go at your own pace remember that youve been able to talk about this with me before and youve made progress as we continue ill periodically ask for a suds rating to check how youre feeling just share your current anxiety level at that moment and well continue dont forget you can always pause if needed

Context: i guess so sure is this about that material you asked me to read about the ways uhm that thinking can trigger anxiety i read about biased thought patterns and remembered something about catastrophizing or filtering and black or white thinking and discounting and several others
Response: exactly ptsd can introduce changes in the way that we think about things and those thoughts can create negative emotional reactions since our last session you got a chance to record some of your selftalk about this issue right lets look at your thoughts about the bank robbery and see if there are any of these biases that may be causing you to stay fearful and avoid reminders of the robbery

Context: i am struggling with thoughts of a traumatic event and i believe that if i think about it or talk about it i will get upset and fall apart just like i did during the incident i end up shaking and crying and its just awful this makes me scared and i tend to avoid thinking about it
Response: i understand that revisiting a traumatic event can be extremely difficult and scary its natural for you to feel scared and avoid thinking about it however its important to recognize that this selftalk is predicting your reaction to the event try to view it as a prediction instead of a certainty facing these thoughts and processing the emotions is an important part of healing and moving forward remember its normal to feel scared but working through the fear is essential for your wellbeing

Context: im feeling nervous about trying the guided self dialogue approach to cope with situations that im avoiding i recognize that although i might panic its not likely that ill lose control but im still nervous that i wont handle it well
Response: its natural to feel nervous about trying something new like guided self dialogue and your acknowledgement shows selfawareness we can break the tasks into four steps and identify coping strategies to make it more manageable now how bad would it actually be if you got nervous or even panicked during this process and what would you want to try to do in those situations

Context: i feel anxious about driving and im afraid that i might panic while on the road to cope i think i would just pull over if it got bad until i could calm down
Response: its good to have a plan for dealing with anxiety on the road if you get too nervous pulling over to calm yourself down can be helpful keep in mind that panicking may not be the most likely outcome but having a plan in place can help put your mind at ease is there anything else related to driving that youre worried about

Context: i have a fear that if i talk or think about a traumatic event i experienced i will lose control and break down however i have talked about it with you and although its not easy and initially made me nervous ive been able to do so without breaking down
Response: youre right about being able to discuss the incident with me without losing control which shows that your fearful prediction is not entirely accurate it seems like you may be experiencing catastrophizing a cognitive bias where you predict worstcase scenarios by recognizing and challenging these biased thoughts you can work towards managing your emotions better when discussing your traumatic experience

Context: i experienced a traumatic event and now i find it hard to talk about it without fear of losing control i keep catastrophizing and its making me avoid talking about the trauma what can i do to overcome this
Response: catastrophizing after a traumatic experience is common and it can cause you to overestimate the likelihood of worstcase scenarios happening while discounting your ability to cope to start overcoming this fear try replacing the thought of losing control with a more accurate thought like even if i cry and shake it will pass i can pull myself together i can face these memories in small steps this will help you gradually confront your trauma and regain control

Context: as a patient when i returned from deployment i found it difficult to adjust to my surroundings feeling like the world was spinning around me i wish for a welcoming environment like someone walking up shaking my hand and saying welcome home brother i also find comfort in connecting with fellow veterans like discussing our experiences while seeing the eagle globe
Response: as a counsellor i understand that adjusting after deployment can be challenging and its important to feel welcomed and supported by your community its great to find comfort in connections with fellow veterans try to attend veteran support groups or engage in activities specifically for veterans to help ease your transition dont hesitate to seek professional help if the feelings become overwhelming

Response: yes having a support system of people who share similar experiences can be very beneficial for coping and healing since you find comfort in being around other marine veterans try seeking out local veterans groups clubs or events where you can connect with them on a more regular basis this could be a positive and impactful way for you to improve your wellbeing

Context: lately ive been participating in the wounded warrior program in my community i know that every program has its positives and negatives but i wanted to explore this program further
Response: its great that youre getting involved in community programs like wounded warrior as you mentioned every program has its pros and cons so its essential to weigh them based on your needs and preferences i encourage you to research more about the program talk to fellow participants and decide if its a good fit for you and if you need any assistance or have any concerns feel free to reach out to me

Context: the three things that really get on my nerves are being asked if i took my meds if i killed anyone and being told thank you instead of saying thank you you suggested saying welcome home in one of our sessions which really resonated with me because it acknowledges the difficulties i went through without being intrusive
Response: im glad that the suggestion of saying welcome home felt more comforting to you as a counsellor its important for me to acknowledge your experiences without making you feel uncomfortable or invalidated i hope others in your life can also learn to be more sensitive and supportive and avoid asking you intrusive questions remember you are home now and its time for you to find healing and solace in a safe environment if theres anything else specific youd like people to say or do let me know

Context: i find myself feeling hopeless and negative about the world and it leads to depression i recall shutting myself in a dark room for the first six months of my sons life and feeling like a failure as a father i have been near gunfire and grenades and i suffer from constant migraines on top of that the medicines i take cause weight gain and ive gained 80 pounds which makes me feel even worse about myself
Response: it seems like you are suffering from posttraumatic stress disorder depression and possibly a traumatic brain injury due to your experiences these conditions can have a major effect on your physical and neurological functioning its important for you to recognize that and not blame yourself have you talked to someone about the possibility of experiencing these conditions and considered seeking treatment options for them

Response: i understand how frustrating it must be to have side effects from the medication especially when you have been dedicated to serving your country and helping your peers its important to remember that adjusting after returning from the military can be challenging so its normal to face some issues have you spoken to your doctor about the side effects and the possibility of adjusting the medication to find a better balance for you

Context: i have taught myself not to feel emotions but i can easily tap into feelings of sadness depression and remorse its hard for me to find joy or see any ray of light except when im with my kids but then i start looking at them and my mind starts taking me to thoughts of possibly taking opportunities away from someone else
Response: it sounds like you are struggling with acknowledging and experiencing positive emotions and instead find it easier to connect with negative feelings like sadness and remorse its good that you feel joy when you are with your kids but its important to address your negative thoughts about possibly taking opportunities away from others have you considered seeking guidance from a therapist who can help you explore these emotions further and develop healthier coping mechanisms

Response: it seems like youre experiencing guilt and remorse about your past military service especially when you see your children enjoying the opportunities that you feel were taken away from others its important to acknowledge these feelings and understand that healing takes time since its been impacting you after the birth of your son have you considered speaking to a therapist or joining a support group for veterans to help process these emotions

Context: ive found that playing guitar has become my selfsoothing technique and it helps me cope with challenges
Response: thats a fantastic selfsoothing technique im really proud of you for finding something that works for you its great to hear that youre able to balance playing guitar with other responsibilities like being a good parent and focusing on your architecture career keep up the good work and remember that im here to support you if you ever need any help or guidance

Context: i have been feeling like a monster looked upon by society because of my experiences as a veteran with ptsd i struggle with people asking me if i killed anybody and it makes me really uncomfortable even when someone thanks me for my service it feels awkward as if i did it for the title of hero or for the glorification
Response: its important to acknowledge the emotional distress youre experiencing due to your experiences as a veteran with ptsd its completely valid to feel uncomfortable when people ask insensitive questions or make assumptions about your intentions i would like to know more about how you cope with these feelings and what support systems you have in place to help you navigate through these difficult situations

Response: i hear that youre struggling with feelings of guilt and undeservingness due to your actions during your service its common for individuals who have experienced trauma or difficult situations to feel this way its essential to recognize your feelings and allow yourself to process them one question id like to ask is have you considered seeking support from a therapist or a support group to help you through this difficult time

Context: ive been attending therapy and working on medication management but im still struggling with my ptsd ive heard about eye movement desensitization and reprocessing emdr and im wondering if it could help me are there any other coping techniques you could recommend
Response: its great that youve been attending therapy and working on medication management as those are essential steps in your recovery emdr can indeed be very helpful for ptsd as it helps reprocess traumatic memories and change your perception of them if you can find a therapist who offers emdr it might be a valuable addition to your treatment plan additionally consider talking with other people who share similar experiences like fellow marines to establish a support network and explore other coping strategies

Context: one thing i learned for self soothing is my marine buddy told me hes like i want you to play guitar that would help me so i started playing about five years ago now i have 12 guitars and i play every day for my kids and i started to research on guitarist rivets and its actually a movement out there of getting vets just to start on guitar
Response: its fantastic to hear that youve found a healthy and enjoyable coping mechanism through playing guitar and that it brings joy to your kids as well the movement you mentioned about involving veterans in guitar playing sounds like a great initiative for supporting mental health keep playing and exploring your passion in music and dont hesitate to reach out if you ever need someone to talk to

Context: i dont really think about suicide but i want to be left alone on an island i dont like being around people crowds and certain cultural aspects but i endure it for my kids at night i cant relax and my mind constantly races with thoughts and scenarios ive recently started medication to help slow my mind down
Response: it seems like youre dealing with a lot of complicated emotions and thoughts its great that youre pushing through these challenges for your kids starting medication is a positive step towards managing your racing thoughts and helping you relax have you noticed any improvements since you started taking the medication

Context: as a patient i struggle with hyper alertness which is a result of my military service its challenging for me to feel secure and at ease even when im in a safe environment
Response: as a counsellor i understand that hyperalertness can be challenging to manage however its important to remember that this is a skill you acquired during your military service and it has its positive aspects as well people around you may appreciate your heightened awareness and ability to detect potential dangers try focusing on the positive aspects of this skill and exploring coping strategies to help manage this alertness in daytoday life

Context: i just finished a therapy session where i had to share my feelings and personal experiences i feel awkward about it
Response: thank you for sharing your feelings with me its completely normal to feel awkward after discussing personal matters in therapy especially if its a new experience for you it might take some time for you to get comfortable with the process however remember that therapy is a safe space for you to express yourself openly is there anything specific that made you feel more awkward or uncomfortable in this session

Response: i appreciate your willingness to be open and help your fellow brothers and sisters its great to see you found value in the three donts for talking to veterans as it can indeed make a significant difference in the way conversations are approached is there any particular aspect of your experience that youre still struggling with or would like to share more about
